questions.question: Objects that shine in the night sky are known as:
questions.solution:
**The Correct Answer is __Option 4__ i.e __celestial bodies__.**

**Celestial bodies:**

__
 
• The **sun, the moon, and all those objects shining** in the night sky are called celestial bodies.
 
• Some **celestial bodies are very big and hot.** They are **made up of gases.**
 
• They have their **own heat and light**, which they emit in large amounts.
 
• These celestial bodies are called **stars**. The sun is a star

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

**__Planets:__**

__
 
• Some celestial bodies **do not have** their **own heat and light.**
 
• They are lit by the light of the stars. Such bodies are called planets.
 
• The word ‘planet’ comes from the **Greek word “Planetai” which means ‘wanderers’.**
 
• The earth on which we live is a planet.
 
• There are eight planets in our solar system.
 
• In order of their distance from the sun, they are **Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.**
 
• It gets all its heat and light from the sun, which is our nearest star.
 
• If we look at the earth from a great distance, say the moon, it will appear to be shining just as the moon

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Satellite:**

__
 
• A Satellite is a celestial body that **moves around the planets** in the same way as the planets move around the sun.

**Asteroid:**

 
• Apart from the stars, planets, and satellites, there are numerous tiny bodies that also move around the sun.
 
• These bodies are called asteroids.
 
• They are found between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter

 
• Meteoroids: A meteoroid is a small rock or particle of debris in our solar system and it burns up as it passes through the Earth's atmosphere, is known as a meteor.
 
• Constellations: Constellation is a group of stars that makes some imaginary shape or pattern in the sky.
 
• Asteroids: A belt of minor planets revolving around the sun between Mars & Jupiter.
 
• **Celestial bodies:**__ It is any natural body outside of the earth's atmosphere.Examples are the Moon, Sun, and the other planets of our solar system.
 
• The term **night sky** refers to the nighttime appearance of **celestial objects** like stars, planets, and the Moon, which are **visible** in a clear sky.

questions.question: Glycolysis occurs in which part of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **1** i.e. __**Cytoplasm**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

**Glycolysis:**

 
• The term glycolysis has originated from the Greek words, **glycos for sugar, and lysis for splitting.**
 
• The scheme of glycolysis was given by **Gustav Embden, Otto Meyerhof, and J. Parnas,** and is often referred to as the **EMP pathway. **
 
• In anaerobic organisms, it is the only process in **respiration. **
 
• Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm of the cell and is present in all** living organisms. **
 
• In this process, glucose undergoes partial oxidation to form two molecules of **pyruvic acid. **
 
• In plants, this glucose is derived from sucrose, which is the end product of photosynthesis, or from **storage carbohydrates. **
 
• Sucrose is converted into **glucose and fructose** by the enzyme, invertase, and these two **monosaccharides **readily enter the **glycolytic pathway. **
 
• **Glucose and fructose** are phosphorylated to give rise to **glucose-6- phosphate** by the activity of the **enzyme hexokinase. **
 
• This phosphorylated form of glucose then isomerizes to produce **fructose-6- phosphate. **
 
• Subsequent steps of metabolism of **glucose and fructose** are the same.
 
• In glycolysis, a chain of **ten reactions**, under the control of different enzymes, takes place to produce **pyruvate from glucose.**

questions.question: Who led the 1662 Mughal expedition against the Ahom Kingdom and captured its capital Garhgaon

__
 
• **Mir Jumla II** was a prominent **general of the Mughal Empire** and served under Emperor **Aurangzeb**.
 
• He led the **1662 Mughal expedition** against the **Ahom Kingdom**, which is located in present-day **Assam**.
 
• The campaign was aimed at expanding Mughal influence in the **Brahmaputra Valley**.
 
• Mir Jumla II successfully captured **Garhgaon**, the **capital of the Ahom Kingdom**, during this campaign.
 
• Despite initial success, the harsh **geography, local resistance, and logistical challenges** made it difficult for the Mughals to maintain a lasting hold on the region.
 
• This campaign is significant in Indian history as it highlights the Mughal Empire’s attempts to expand its territories into the **northeastern region** of India.
 
• Mir Jumla II was also a **statesman and a skilled administrator**, contributing significantly to the Mughal Empire’s governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He played a key role in the **Rajput-Mughal alliance** and led campaigns in **Bengal, Orissa, and the Deccan**.
 
• Man Singh is not associated with the Ahom expedition.

 __

questions.question: What is the essential element that is suitable during the synthesis of proteins and other compounds in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nitrogen **is a crucial element for the **synthesis of proteins **and other compounds in plants.
 
• It is a major component of chlorophyll, the compound plants use in photosynthesis.
 
• Nitrogen is also a significant part of amino acids, the** building blocks of proteins**.
 
• Plants absorb nitrogen primarily in the form of **nitrate (NO₃⁻) and ammonium (NH₄⁺)** ions from the soil.
 
• Deficiency of nitrogen in plants can lead to stunted growth and yellowing of leaves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron:**

 
 
• Iron is essential for the synthesis of chlorophyll and is involved in some enzymatic processes.
 
• It plays a vital role in the electron transport chain in photosynthesis.
 
• Iron deficiency can cause chlorosis, where leaves turn yellow while veins remain green.
 
 
 
• **Phosphorus:**
 
 
• Phosphorus is important for energy transfer in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate).
 
• It is also essential for the formation of DNA and RNA.
 
• Phosphorus deficiency can lead to poor root growth and delayed maturity.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen:**
 
 
• Oxygen is essential for cellular respiration in plants.
 
• It is required for the breakdown of carbohydrates to produce energy.
 
• Oxygen is also a byproduct of photosynthesis.

questions.question: An object that weighs 60 kg on Earth will weigh approximately how much on the Moon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 kg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The weight of an object depends on the **gravitational force** acting on it.
 
• The **gravitational force** on the Moon is approximately **1/6th** that of Earth's gravitational force.
 
• Since the object weighs **60 kg** on Earth, its weight on the Moon will be approximately **60 ÷ 6 = 10 kg**.
 
• While the **mass** of the object remains constant regardless of location, its **weight** changes due to varying gravitational forces.
 
• The formula to calculate weight is **W = mg**, where **m** is mass and **g** is gravitational acceleration.
 
• On Earth, the acceleration due to gravity (**g**) is approximately **9.8 m/s²**, while on the Moon, it is around **1.6 m/s²**.
 
• This principle is crucial in **space exploration** and understanding the behavior of objects on celestial bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **60 kg**__

 __
 
• **Mass** and **weight** are different concepts. The mass of an object remains the same everywhere, but its weight depends on the **gravitational force**.
 
• If the object weighs **60 kg** on Earth, it will not weigh the same on the Moon because of the difference in gravity.
 
 
 
• **30 kg**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because the **Moon's gravity** is not half of Earth's gravity. It is approximately **1/6th** of Earth's gravity.
 
 
 
• **5 kg**__
 
 
• This value does not align with the calculation based on the Moon's gravitational force, which is **1/6th** of Earth's gravity.
